transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A persistent smell after cleaning is rarely just 'dirt' left behind; it usually means something is trapped where you can't easily reach it. The most common culprit is the defrost drain at the back of the freezer or fridge compartment—if this gets blocked by food debris or ice, stagnant water and mould build up there, circulating a musty odour every time the fan runs. However, if the smell is sharp, like burning plastic or rubber, that suggests an electrical component overheating, which needs immediate attention. To give you the best advice on how to clear it safely, I need to know exactly what we are dealing with. Could you tell me the brand and model number of your fridge-freezer? It’s usually on a sticker inside the cabinet, often on a side wall near the salad drawer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

It's a Beko, model CDA543FS. I read it off the label inside the fridge. The smell is a bit like hot plastic or electrical burning, more at the back than inside. There's also an occasional buzzing from the back.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning plastic smell combined with buzzing from the back of your Beko CDA543FS suggests an electrical component failure—most likely the compressor start relay, internal wiring insulation breaking down, or the compressor itself overheating. Because this involves live mains voltage and potential fire risk, you must stop using the appliance immediately and leave it unplugged until a qualified engineer has inspected it. Do not attempt to open the back panel yourself; the sealed system and electrical components are dangerous if handled incorrectly. Please contact Beko customer support or a certified repair technician for a safe diagnosis.

candidates: Food spoilage or organic matter trapped in the drain or seals (high)
Mould or mildew in the air circulation system (low)
